correctness.rationale: For a Haar direction in dimension three, |u_z| is uniform on [0,1]. Taking the forward and reverse supports of the filled-base cone yields W/r=√(1−z²)+max(√(1−z²),tz), split at z=(1+t²)^(−1/2). Integrating on the two intervals gives exactly a/2 and b/3 for the first and second normalized moments. I independently differentiated 4b/(3a²)−1 and the reduced T symbolically; the positive-factor derivative and the P,Q radical identity in equations (4) and (5) both hold. On 0<t≤3 the numerator is strictly negative, bounded by P−Q when P≤0 and by 4P−Q otherwise. For t≥3 the stated root and Bernoulli bounds yield T<π/2+3/2<π: the required polynomial t³+t²−19t/2−4 is positive at 3 and strictly increasing thereafter. At the other end T~16/(5t). Thus the derivative sign changes exactly once, from negative to positive. At √3, T=π/3+6√3/5<π, putting the unique root strictly below √3. The width extremes themselves follow by testing the branch junction, the endpoint values t and 2, and the concave second branch maximum √(1+t²) if its stationary point lies on the branch: they give the stated two-piece worst-ratio profile and unique minimizer √3. Continuity on the sphere identifies extrema with essential extrema. Independent 70-digit arithmetic gave t*=1.70901306660551564276 and squared CV 0.00168696607831620408958. The frozen finite checker was inspected but not run; only the analytic inequalities justify global uniqueness.

originality.rationale: The retained distinct claim is the exact global cone CV optimization and its strict separation from the known worst-width optimum. The earlier full cone-width density is stronger for distributional questions, so the elementary moment formulas and the worst-ratio result do not receive independent originality credit. Neither that prior nor the same-day squared-CV optimization for another family supplies the cone minimizer or its global uniqueness reasoning in the inspected evidence.
residual_risks: An earlier calculation may be unindexed or included under other width-anisotropy terminology. The checked density already makes the numerical objective derivable.
The cited Schneider full text was not available; unrelated results from a broader query are not negative evidence.

value.rationale: Squared relative variation is an intrinsic scale-free loss for uniform directions. Finding the exact unique aspect ratio over the whole natural solid-cone family, and showing it differs strictly from the cone minimizing worst-direction variation, reveals an objective-dependent choice of shape that cannot be inferred merely from the old width-range optimum. The global comparison rather than the decimal approximation is the substantial content.
